title: Around is not across
hook: A perimeter measurement and a corner-to-corner measurement follow different paths.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Select the correct length formula for boundary versus corner-to-corner routes.

misconception: Every measurement associated with a rectangle is its perimeter.
objective: Select the correct length formula for boundary versus corner-to-corner routes.

claims.text: An ideal rectangle is 4m wide and 3m high. Compare one full perimeter with one diagonal. Scaled model; ideal rectangle; length only.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Width=4m, A=14m and B=5m. The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",2,["+","x",3]]; B=["sqrt",["+",["*","x","x"],9]]; x denotes Width. At x=4, A=14, B=5; recall at x=7: B=7.61577310586. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: Perimeter adds all four edges. The diagonal follows one straight corner-to-corner path and uses the square-root relationship. Name the route before calculating the required length; the same rectangle supports different measurements.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",2,["+","x",3]]; B=["sqrt",["+",["*","x","x"],9]]; x denotes Width. At x=4, A=14, B=5; recall at x=7: B=7.61577310586. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: An ideal rectangle is 4m wide and 3m high. Compare one full perimeter with one diagonal. Change only Width to 7m. What is B (Diagonal) now? Correct: 7.616m. Use B's stated rule with Width=7m: it gives 7.616m. Perimeter adds all four edges. The diagonal follows one straight corner-to-corner path and uses the square-root relationship. Name the route before calculating the required length; the same rectangle supports different measurements.

recall.question: An ideal rectangle is 4m wide and 3m high. Compare one full perimeter with one diagonal. Change only Width to 7m. What is B (Diagonal) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Width=7m: it gives 7.616m. Perimeter adds all four edges. The diagonal follows one straight corner-to-corner path and uses the square-root relationship. Name the route before calculating the required length; the same rectangle supports different measurements.

safety.assumptions: An ideal rectangle is 4m wide and 3m high. Compare one full perimeter with one diagonal.
safety.excluded: No chemical mixtures, medical advice, wiring, safety-device bypass, actual tariffs, financial recommendations, temperature, food-storage or food-safety instructions. All energy powers, durations and tariffs are illustrative.
